### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**10** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/index.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class), auditMissingTenant (symbol, a method of class SqlDriver), buildDriverOptions (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL), bulkCreate (symbol, a method of class SqlDriver), bulkCreate (literal, a string literal in bulkCreate))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1eb1afae071530f66f4d93d416e7f452ceab3de3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e5150730fb8d51cc44a0dfab3026cba84403a8fe` — the merge of head `1313821b578acc2702e364c74aac8c7b1400b4b5` into base `1eb1afae071530f66f4d93d416e7f452ceab3de3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e5150730fb8d51cc44a0dfab3026cba84403a8fe && git checkout e5150730fb8d51cc44a0dfab3026cba84403a8fe
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1eb1afae071530f66f4d93d416e7f452ceab3de3 1313821b578acc2702e364c74aac8c7b1400b4b5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1eb1afae071530f66f4d93d416e7f452ceab3de3 && git merge --no-ff 1313821b578acc2702e364c74aac8c7b1400b4b5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1eb1afae071530f66f4d93d416e7f452ceab3de3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1eb1afae071530f66f4d93d416e7f452ceab3de3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Reviewed at 2026-10-22T19:35Z. Inputs: card #25230 (body, claim 6347729103, dev report 6349387651), record 6341425088 on #25210 (③ item 3 only), this PR's body, file list and net diff against its merge base `0f1eeeeeb`, and the check-runs on the head. Read from git and the REST API only. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**The head moved after the dev report.** The report and the review brief both name `d323330402`. The PR head is `0d69599888`, a ninth file pushed at 2026-10-22T19:27Z by the same dev session: `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`, +17/−9. This record reviews `0d69599888`. Its code is byte-identical to `d323330402`; the only change is the docs page.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Diagnostics only, no write behaviour change: RIGHT.**
   - **Where the exemption is decided.** It is decided once, in `buildDriverOptions`, as `wallExempt = tenantObject && isTenantAuditInScope && !scope.writeTarget && wallExemptedOperation(execCtx, scope.recordedVerdict)`. `wallExemptedOperation` returns true only when two things hold. First, the recorded verdict parses as `TenantLayer0VerdictSchema` with `kind: 'none'`. Second, `engineLayer0Verdict` (the engine's existing fallback, now extracted with the same inputs: `objectHasOrgIdField: undefined`, `posturePermitsCrossTenant: false`, `isPlatformAdmin: false`) does not answer `none`.
   - **The extraction does not change the fallback.** `driverReadScope` calls the extracted helper with the same arguments the inline call had, so read and write scope are unchanged.
   - **Every reader of `bypassTenantAudit`.** A `git grep` over non-test source in `packages/**` finds one driver reader: `sql-driver.ts:16108`, an early `return` inside `auditMissingTenant`, before the warn. It changes no filter, no stamp and no refusal.
     - `driver-turso` and `driver-sqlite-wasm` inherit that method.
     - `driver-memory` and `driver-mongodb` have no reader and no audit.
     - Every other hit is a writer: the engine itself, service-settings, service-messaging, service-datasource. Or it is the pass-through key list at `engine.ts:607`.
   - **No new `OperationContext` member and no `DriverOptions` key.** The diff touches no interface. The driver adds no posture read; `isMultiTenantMode()` was already there.
   - **The changed early return.** It now also skips returning `base` when `wallExempt` is true. The only effect is a shallow copy of `base` that carries `bypassTenantAudit: true`. That is the same copy every other branch already makes.
   - **Traced: cases where the flag is not set.**
     - *A tenant user under a wall.* The recorded verdict is `organization`, `organizations` or `deny`, so the answer is false.
     - *An isSystem write.* plugin-security's middleware returns `next()` for `context.isSystem` (`security-plugin.ts:2561`) before step 3 records anything, so the recorded verdict is `undefined` and the answer is false. The D13 cut is untouched. An out-of-scope object is still muted by the existing branch, and an in-scope one still warns.
     - *A federated or tenancy-disabled object.* `tenantObject` is false.
     - *An insert.* It is built with `{ writeTarget: true }` (`engine.ts:17276`).
     - *A by-id write and the cascade delete* (`engine.ts:21730`). Neither passes a recorded verdict.
     - *A delegated write.* `intersectTenantLayer0Verdicts` of the admin's `none` with the delegator's wall is a wall.
     - *The #12974 owner bypass.* It records `none` on reads only. There the flag is inert, because the driver reads it only in the write-op audit.
     - *Posture.* The posture provider the engine reads is the one plugin-security hands it, so whenever a verdict was recorded, the two sides ask the same posture.

2. **driver-sql insert skip: RIGHT.**
   - **The two insert doors.** `create` passes `[toInsert]` before `injectTenantOnInsert`. `bulkCreate` moves its audit call after the id-assignment `map` and before injection, and passes every row.
   - **The skip condition.** The skip needs `insertRows.length > 0 && insertRows.every(carriesTenant)`, so one row without the column keeps the line. An empty `bulkCreate` keeps the line too, as before.
   - **What counts as carrying.** "Carries" means not `undefined`, not `null` and not `''`. That is the exact spelling `injectTenantOnInsert` uses, so a row with `organization_id: null` still warns. A non-object row counts as not carrying.
   - **Other ops are unchanged.** `update` (9061), `upsert` (9753), `delete` (10114), `bulkDelete` (10383), `updateMany` (10442) and `deleteMany` (10483) pass no rows, so they warn as before.
   - **The line is unchanged.** The warn string and its meta object are not in the diff, so the `[tenant-audit] OP on tenant-scoped object "OBJECT" without options.tenantId` prefix is byte-identical. That keeps service-messaging's `delivery-claim-tenant-audit.integration.test.ts:64` and `delivery-update-tenant-audit.integration.test.ts:97` matching.

3. **Tests: RIGHT. One fixture move, one swap that strengthens a test, no assertion weakened.**
   - **`sql-driver-tenant-audit-posture.test.ts`.**
     - `writeWithoutTenant` was a `create` whose row carried `organization_id`. It is now a by-id `delete`. Every `true` and `false` expectation is unchanged; the first one's meta now names `op: 'delete'`.
     - The `bypassTenantAudit` case moved from a create to a delete. On the old shape that case would have passed with or without the bypass at this head, so the move strengthens it.
     - The updateMany text test only re-seeds its row with a direct `create`.
   - **`sql-driver-tenant-scope.test.ts`.** The throttle pin swaps two creates for two deletes. The assertion is unchanged: one warn per `object:op`.
   - **Do the new pins go red without the fix?**
     - In the driver file, the `create` and `bulkCreate` "no line" pins depend only on the new `every(carriesTenant)` return. Delete it and both print a line, so both go red; the 9 controls do not depend on it.
     - In the engine file, the three "declared" pins assert `bypassTenantAudit === true` on a recorded `none`, and nothing else in `buildDriverOptions` sets it for a non-system context on a tenant object. Remove the assignment and all three go red; the 7 "not declared" pins stay green.
     - That reasoning matches both ablations the dev reports (2/9 and 3/7).

4. **Measurement: PLAUSIBLE against the code.**
   - **The insert lines.** At a walled seed boot the inserts are system context, refused above the driver when they carry no organization (D9), so each one that reaches the driver carries `organization_id`. That fits 32 → 0 for `create` and `bulkCreate`.
   - **The update lines.** The 5 `update` and 18 `updateMany` lines are isSystem seed writes. They record no verdict, so they get no exemption and still warn, as the card requires.
   - **The counts.** The throttle is per `object:op`, so the counts are distinct object/op pairs, not write totals.
   - **Nothing still warns that the Acceptance says should not.** The exemption half is pinned at the `DriverOptions` seam only. The PR body states `NOT MEASURED: live exempt-admin predicate write`, which the card's Acceptance does not require.

5. **The docs commit (`tenant-audit-census.mdx`): the sentences are RIGHT; the commit is the conflict below.**
   - Checked sentence by sentence, the new guard list is true of this head: the D13 isSystem cut, the D8 exemption fill-in, guard 6 for insert rows, and "thread an elevated one and an object with a tenant column is still audited, unless…".
   - It answers the docs-drift comment and the stale lines 49-50 that record 6341425088 ③2 named.
   - It is not in the dev report's `files_changed` (8 files), and the report's 74/74 gate run was taken on `d323330402`, not on this file.

### ② Semver level

RIGHT.
- Two `patch` changesets: `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/objectql`. Both packages are published (`private` unset, 18.0.0).
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in the PR body and in both changeset bodies. No `(narrowing)` arm, and no BREAKING banner is owed.
- `Clause-②: no` holds. `packages/spec` is untouched, so `DriverOptions`, `OperationContext` and `TenantLayer0VerdictSchema` do not move. The only exported-class signature change is an optional trailing parameter on the `protected` `SqlDriver.auditMissingTenant`, which existing overrides and callers still satisfy. The new engine methods are `private`.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: nothing an author can write moves.
- `Check Changeset` succeeded on `d323330402`, which carries the same two changesets. It has not run on this head (see FAIL item 1).

### ③ Boundary flags

**FAIL item 1: the head conflicts with `main`, and no check-run exists on it.**
- **The conflict.** `main`'s `24360dcfb` (#25266) rewrote bullet 2 of `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` (the isSystem mute is now schema-cut), and `0d69599888` rewrites the same lines. GitHub reports `mergeable: false`, `mergeable_state: dirty`.
- **No CI.** `GET commits/0d69599888…/check-runs` answers `total_count: 0`. CI on the head is unmeasurable.
- **This PR caused it.** `d323330402` does not touch the file and merged cleanly; the conflict arrived with this PR's own last commit.
- **Fix.** Merge `main`. Resolve bullet 2 so it keeps main's D13 wording and adds this PR's D8 clause. Then let the full check set run on the new head and re-report the gates for it.
- **What this record does not cover.** The code judgments above do not change on that merge if it touches only the docs page. Even so, this record does not cover a new head.

**Check-run tally at posting:**
- Head `0d69599888`: 0 runs.
- For reference, not counted: the superseded `d323330402` has 39 runs — 24 success, 7 skipped, 8 in_progress (`Test Core (1/6)`–`(6/6)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`). Of the five required contexts there, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` succeeded; `Test Core` and the type-check lanes had not finished.

**Dev deviations: both ACCEPTED.**
- The attribution line links the card thread. The line is the platform's, and the card reference `Fixes #25230` is the first content line. It sits beside no other open card's number, and `Part of #15212` carries no closing keyword.
- The skipped MCP reviewer request: the order forbids MCP writes, and the assignee rode `pr_create`.

**Observations, not blocking:**
- (a) There is no dedicated `organization_id: null` pin. `undefined` (missing key) and `''` are pinned, and `null` is correct by reading. A one-line control would make it explicit.
- (b) `wallExemptedOperation` is "recorded `none` where the engine's fallback walls". It is not the literal `crossedByPlatformAdmin` test, which also needs `isPlatformAdmin`. The two differ only where plugin-security's `objectHasOrgIdField` (it checks for `organization_id`) and the engine's `resolveTenantFieldName` (a declared `tenancy.tenantField`) disagree. An example is an object named in `platformGlobalObjects` that declares its own tenant field. On such an object the wall itself returned `none` and the effect is one silenced warning, so this is diagnostics only.
